title: Decorations with ::before and ::after
summary: Pseudo-elements add a required asterisk, an external-link arrow and quote marks without touching the markup.
explanation: ::before and ::after create an extra box inside the element, before or after its content. They only appear when they have a content property, even an empty one (content: "").

Here they add decoration that belongs to the style, not the text: a red asterisk after required labels, an arrow after links that leave the site, and curly quotes around a quotation. Change the CSS and every one updates.
Screen readers may or may not read generated content, so never put important information only in content. The word required is also in the label's aria attribute here.
tryThis: Remove content from .external::after: the arrow disappears even though the rest of the rule is still there.
Change the quote marks to « and ».

children.text: Make it work, make it right, make it fast.
